name: Arkansas
summary: A red field with a white diamond bordered in blue, containing four blue stars and the word 'ARKANSAS', with 25 white stars in the border. Designed by Willie Hocker for the Daughters of the American Revolution in 1913.
origin: Willie Hocker, a schoolteacher, won a 1912 contest held by the Daughters of the American Revolution. The legislature adopted the flag in 1913. A fourth star for the Confederacy was added in 1923, and the stars were rearranged in 1924.

symbols.name: Diamond
symbols.description: A white diamond in the centre.
symbols.meaning: Arkansas as the only US state producing diamonds.

symbols.name: Twenty-five stars
symbols.description: White stars in the blue border.

symbols.name: Three lower stars
symbols.meaning: The three nations that ruled the area: Spain, France and the US; also 1803 (Louisiana Purchase) and Arkansas as the third state from it.

symbols.name: Upper star
symbols.description: A blue star above the name.

facts: Crater of Diamonds State Park lets visitors dig for diamonds.
Its design echoes the Confederate battle flag's colours and star border.
clues: A white diamond with blue stars and the state name, on red with a star border.
Its diamond shape refers to a precious stone mined in the state.
Its 25 stars show it was the 25th state.
